sections.title: 一、詞彙與慣用語(15%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第1至15題，每題選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

questions.stem: I called the airline to ______ my flight reservation a week before I left for Canada.

The organic food products are made of natural ingredients, with no ______ flavors added.
Jessica is a very religious girl; she believes that she is always ______ supported by her god.
Jane usually buys things on ______. Her purchases seem to be driven by some sudden force or desire.
The week-long rainfall has ______ landslides and flooding in the mountain areas.

sections.title: 二、綜合測驗(15%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第16至30題，每題一個空格，請依文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage: Whenever a Dalai Lama died, a search began for his reincarnation. The [[16]] male child had to have certain qualities. [[17]] was the ability to identify the belongings of his predecessor, or rather his previous self. Another requirement was [[18]] he should have large ears, upward-slanting eyes and eyebrows. Besides, one of his hands should bear a mark like a conch-shell. The successful candidate, usually [[19]] two or three, was then removed from his family to Lhasa to begin spiritual training for his future role. The Panchen Lamas were chosen in a similar way. The reincarnated leaders were always “discovered” in the households of lowly families [[20]] noble ones. This was to ensure that no single and powerful noble family could seize the title and pass it to the next generation.

groups.passage: Learning style means a person’s natural, habitual, and preferred way(s) of learning. Research about learning styles has identified [[26]] differences. sections.title: 三、文意選填(10%)
sections.instructions: 說明：第31至40題，每題一個空格，請依文意在文章後所提供的 (A) 到 (J) 選項中分別選出最適當者，並將其英文字母代號標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得1分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage:
Although stories about aliens have never been officially confirmed, their existence has been widely speculated upon.
Many people believe that [[31]] from outer space have visited us for centuries. Some say that life on Earth [[32]] “out there” and was seeded here. Others say that aliens have [[33]] what happens on Earth, and are responsible for quite a few legends, and that the ancient Greek and Roman gods, [[34]] the fairies and dwarfs in many classical tales, were in fact “space people” living here. Still [[35]] say that aliens were responsible for the growth of highly evolved civilizations which have [[36]] perished, including the Incan and Mayan civilizations and the legendary Atlantis.
A lot of ancient civilizations, [[37]] the Egyptians, Hindus, Greeks, and Mayans, have left writings and [[38]] which indicate contacts with superior beings “from the stars.” Many believe that the aliens are here to help us, while others hold that the aliens intend us [[39]]. Still others think that most aliens visit Earth to study us like our scientists study primitive natives and animals, and have no interest in helping us [[40]].
It is difficult to comment conclusively on these theories in general, apart from saying that any and all of them might be possible. Maybe time will tell.

sections.title: 四、閱讀測驗(30%)
sections.instructions: 說明︰第41至55題，每題請分別根據各篇文章之文意選出最適當的一個選項，標示在答案卡之「選擇題答案區」。每題答對得2分，答錯不倒扣。

groups.passage: A sense of humor is just one of the many things shared by Alfred and Anthony Melillo, 64-year-old twin brothers from East Haven who made history in February 2002. On Christmas Eve, 1992, Anthony had a heart transplant from a 21-year-old donor. Two days before Valentine’s Day in 2002, Alfred received a 19-year-old heart, marking the first time on record that twin adults each received heart transplants. “I’m 15 minutes older than him, but now I’m younger because of my heart and I’m not going to respect him,” Alfred said with a grin, pointing to his brother while talking to a roomful of reporters, who laughed frequently at their jokes. While the twins knew that genetics might have played a role in their condition, they recognized that their eating habits might have also contributed to their heart problems. “We’d put half a pound of butter on a steak. I overdid it on all the food that tasted good, so I guess I deserved what I got for not dieting properly.” The discussion moved to Anthony’s recovery. In the five years since his heart transplant, he had been on an exercise program where he regularly rode a bicycle for five miles, swam each day, and walked a couple of miles. He was still on medication, but not nearly as much as Alfred, who was just in the early stage of his recovery. “Right now I feel pretty young and I’m doing very well,” Anthony said. “I feel like a new person.” Alfred said his goal, of course, was to feel even better than his brother. But, he added, “I love my brother very much. We’re very close and I’m sure we’ll do just fine.”

groups.passage: In 1993, the Metropolitan Museum of Art reluctantly handed over 363 pieces of gold, silver, precious stones, paintings, and sculptures back to Turkey after a court case. Following increasing calls for the return of artistic objects that were removed decades or centuries ago, some of the world’s leading museums have signed a declaration that they will not hand back the ancient artifacts to their countries of origin. They say people all over the world have only been able to fully appreciate ancient civilizations because these museums have provided access to these artistic objects. The ancient civilizations would not be so deeply admired today if these ancient artifacts were not so widely available to an international public in major museums throughout Europe and America. For example, Egyptian culture would not have become so well-known if the museums had not put Egyptian mummies on show. The British Museum has not signed the declaration, but says it fully supports it. Over the recent years, it has faced growing pressure to hand back the Elgin Marbles, sculptures taken from the Parthenon in Athens, Greece, in the 19th century. But the British Museum has said that the Museum is the best possible place for them. “They must remain here if the museum is to continue to achieve its aim, which is to show the world to the world,” said the director of the museum.

groups.passage:
Some animals have organs in their bodies that produce light. When it is dark, they flash their lights on and off to signal to others of their species, to lure prey toward them, or to escape from predators.
Some fish are found to produce light in the blackness of the sea. When night falls over the Red Sea, tiny flashlight fish rise to the surface for food, each with a pair of “headlamps,” one beneath each eye. With the light produced by bacteria living there, they communicate with other flashlight fish to avoid getting too close to each other, so that the fish may spread out evenly to get enough food. And if a flashlight fish is threatened by a predator, it swims away in a zigzag path, flashing its light on and off very quickly to confuse the animal pursuing it.
Certain land animals can also produce light. Fireflies, small beetles that live in many warmer parts of the world, use light to attract a mate. After darkness falls in some parts of North America, female fireflies gather on the ground. The males fly overhead, flashing light from the undersides of their bodies. As there are a number of species of firefly, the males of each kind flash their own particular signal. Recognizing the flashing code of her own species, a female signals back to the male, and he lands beside her.
On land as in the sea, living lights can be deceiving. When they are hungry, some female fireflies lure the males of other species to them. They flash a false response when these males signal overhead, but eat them when they land.

options.C: Male fireflies may deceive females with false signals.
options.D: Female fireflies respond from the ground to males’ signals.

tags.topic: animals that produce light (flashlight fish and fireflies)

passage_parts.title: Brooks, Bruce. Everywhere. HarperCollins, 1990. ISBN0060207299. 70 pages.
passage_parts.text: Peanuts’ beloved grandfather has suffered a heart attack. Peanuts is sad over the possibility of losing his grandfather. Dooley keeps Peanuts company while the adults in the family attend to Grandfather. Dooley attempts to save the old man by a ritual learned from comic books: killing a turtle and trading his soul for Grandfather’s. With the imaginative assistance of Dooley, Peanuts discovers the healing power of hope and love.

passage_parts.title: Babbitt, Natalie. Tuck Everlasting. Farrar, 1975. ISBN0374378487. 180 pages.
passage_parts.text: The Tuck family has discovered a spring whose water brings eternal life. A man learns their secret and threatens to sell the water to the highest bidder. Mrs. Tuck kills the man and is jailed and sentenced to be executed. Though the family knows she cannot be killed, they worry that their secret will be revealed when they try to kill her.

passage_parts.title: Baylor, Byrd. The Table Where Rich People Sit. Simon & Schuster, 1994. ISBN0684196530. 52 pages.
passage_parts.text: Around an old kitchen table, a young girl calls a family meeting to show her parents that they should earn more money so they can have nicer things. As she points out they are not sitting at a table where rich people would sit, her parents calculate the value of the desert hills, the blooming cactus, the calls of eagles, and one another’s company. Soon, she realizes that her poor family is rich in things that matter in life. She concludes that this is indeed a table where rich people sit.

passage_parts.title: Goble, Paul. Beyond the Ridge. Bradbury, 1989. ISBN0027365816. 32 pages.
passage_parts.text: There is no death; only a change of worlds—the author delivers these reassurances to readers in this book, based on the customs of the Plains Indians in America. The book reads like a prayer, expressing specific beliefs about dying. It describes a woman who is called by her long-dead mother to go “beyond the ridge.” After a steep climb, she discovers a world that is abundantly beautiful, and there she finds the familiar faces of people who have passed that way before her.

extraction.method: Word 版 (paper-2.doc → soffice 轉 docx → python-docx) 為主要文字來源，與 pdftotext -layout 題本以程式逐詞比對；Read 看題本 PDF 全部 8 頁影像確認版面、粗體／斜體／底線與題組，docx run 格式核對底線位置；第 8 頁作文連環圖以 pdftoppm 400/800dpi 放大裁切後人工描述；答案取自 answer.pdf 第 2 頁英文考科（多科合併檔，pdftotext＋頁面影像核對）；統計取自 stats-1.xls（P/Ph/Pl/D）與 stats-2.xls（全體考生 T 列選項比例），並程式核對 stats-2 標星號選項＝官方答案、D＝Ph−Pl。；查證（verifier）：答案逐題對照 answer.pdf 第 2 頁影像、選文／題幹／選項／書目以程式對照 pdftotext 與 Word 版逐字比對、統計 55 題全數對照 stats-1／stats-2、題本 8 頁影像與作文連環圖 300／600dpi 放大重新核對。
issues: 結構核對：與 gsat-spec.json legacy_gsat「93」期別一致（詞彙與慣用語1–15題共15分、綜合測驗16–30題共15分〔3篇×5題〕、文意選填31–40題10分〔A–J〕、閱讀測驗41–55題每題2分共30分〔4篇，題數依序為4、3、4、4〕；翻譯題2題×5分共10分、英文作文20分；選擇題70分／非選擇題30分），作文文長「120個單詞(words)左右」與 essay_length_by_year「91-94,96-98」相符，無不一致。題本封面：考試時間100分鐘、第壹部分單一選擇題共55題、第貳部分非選擇題共2大題、選擇題答錯不倒扣。
評分原則：本年度 units.json 沒有 scoring（非選擇題評分原則）檔，翻譯題 answer／accepted_answers／scoring_notes 與作文 scoring_notes 一律填 null（未自行作答）；也沒有非選擇題得分分布統計，翻譯與作文的 stats 填 null。
題號：題本翻譯題印為 1、2，作文無題號；比照 gsat-94／96／97 慣例，no 接續選擇題依序為 56、57（翻譯）、58（作文），題本原編號保留在 label「翻譯1」「翻譯2」「作文」。56–58 並非題本印刷題號。
Word 自動編號：Word 版中第42、44–47、49–51、53–55題的題號、文意選填選項庫的「(A)」、翻譯題標題的「一、」及翻譯題的「1.」「2.」都是自動編號（不在文字裡），已依 PDF 題本補回或對齊；翻譯題大題標題依 PDF「一 、 翻 譯 題 (10%)」寫成「一、翻譯題(10%)」。part 取題本「第壹部分：單一選擇題」「第貳部分：非選擇題」的部分名稱。

中文說明比對：大題標題、說明、翻譯題、作文提示取自 Word 版，並與 pdftotext 題本（先把 ㈻㆒㊜㊠㉃㆗ 等舊版相容字元換回一般字，再忽略空白）逐字比對，結果一致。冒號照原文保留：一、二、四大題說明、作文說明與「提示︰」用「︰」(U+FE30)，三大題與翻譯題說明用「：」(U+FF1A)。翻譯第1題 Word 版是「雖然Lily生來」，Lily 前後沒有空白（PDF 排版顯示的間距是中英文自動間距）；作文提示「以“One evening,…”開頭」也一樣，都依 Word 版不加空白。
文字來源比對：Word 版（paper-2.doc → soffice 轉 docx）與 pdftotext 題本的全部英文內容（選文、題幹、選項、選項庫、書目）以程式逐詞比對，共 2801 個詞（含標點），完全一致。

空白正規化：Word／PDF 中排版造成的連續空白、Tab 已壓成單一空白；題幹中的底線空格長度照原文保留（第12、49、50題為 5 個底線，第41題為 9 個，其他為 6 個）。第24題原文「the most__(24)__ areas」空格前沒有空白，照原文寫成「most[[24]] areas」；第44題題幹結尾「my heart” ?」問號前有空白，照原文保留。52–55 書目第三則在 PDF 中「52」與「pages.」換行，已合併為一行。

照原文保留：21–25 選文「malaria－Cambodia’s」的破折號在 Word 版與 PDF 都是全形連字號「－」(U+FF0D)，照原樣保留；52–55 第四則「worlds—the」為 em dash。41–44 選文說 Anthony 在 1992 年聖誕夜換心、2002 年接受訪問，卻寫「In the five years since his heart transplant」，年數與日期對不上，屬原文內容，照錄不改。PDF 第4頁（題本第3頁）第一段「heart transplants.」後方遠處有一個極小的點，Word 版與 pdftotext 都沒有，判定為印刷斑點，不收錄。

格式標記：第47題問的是畫底線的字。選文「show the world to the world」整句粗體，第一個 the world 加底線，選文寫成 show the world to the world；第47題題幹「“the world”」與「“show the world to the world”」的第一個 the world 也加底線（已用 docx run 格式與頁面影像確認），題幹以 the world 標出。題目問到的粗體也在選文以 標出並填 refers_to：41–44 選文第2段開頭引語 “I’m 15 minutes older than him, but now I’m younger because of my heart”（第44題）、45–47 選文的 countries of origin（第46題）；題幹的粗體不加標記。其餘粗體與斜體不保留：52–55 書名為粗體；21–25 選文兩處 The CAMBODIA DAILY 的 The 為斜體。各題組前的「41-44 為題組」等標示（粗體加底線）是版面標題，沒有放進 passage。

52–55 書目：題本用一個方框框住四則書目，各則之間以虛線分隔，沒有 A–D 標號。passage_parts 的 label 填 null，title 放每則第一行的書目（作者、書名、出版社、出版年、ISBN、頁數，原文書名為粗體），text 放下方簡介；虛線沒有收錄。figures 另以 rows 整理四則書目的作者／書名／出版社／出版年／ISBN／頁數，因為第52、53題要比較頁數和出版年。原文「ISBN0060207299」的 ISBN 與號碼之間沒有空白，照原文保留。

統計：correct_rate／high_group／low_group／discrimination 取自 stats-1.xls 英文工作表（P、Ph、Pl、D），option_rates 取自 stats-2.xls 英文工作表全體考生（T 列）。已用程式核對：stats-2 標星號的選項全部等於官方答案，D＝Ph−Pl 全部成立。答案選項比例與 stats-1 不同的有三題：第36題 P 為 15%、stats-2 的 I 為 16%；第28題 Pl 為 27%、stats-2 L 列的 B 為 28%；第49題 Pl 為 32%、stats-2 L 列的 A 為 33%，應是四捨五入造成，一律採用 stats-1。option_rates 不含「未答」欄（0–1%），因四捨五入，部分題目加總為 0.98–1.01。stats-1 另有五等分組 Pa–Pe、D1–D4，stats-2 另有高／低分組（H、L 列）各選項比例，schema 沒有對應欄位，未收錄。

作文圖畫：三張連環圖以文字描述，放在 s6g1.figures（kind=picture），描述根據 400／800dpi 放大的頁面影像人工撰寫；caption 是描述用的標題（題本的圖沒有編號）。「囍」「Gulp」「TAXI!」「XX警察局」「POLICE」「!?」是圖中印的文字。第1張穿亮片長禮服的女子判斷為新娘；第2張左側大型車輛的車頂燈和第3張窗外警車的警示燈畫法相近，但題本沒有說明車種，所以只描述看得到的內容。作文沒有要求段數，tags 不填 paragraphs；提示要求以 “One evening,…” 開頭，並「提供合理的解釋與結局」。

標註判斷：s2g2（CAMBODIA DAILY 防瘧疾蚊帳募款）是募款廣告，genre 標 advertisement，sdgs 標 3；s2g3（學習風格的性別差異）sdgs 標 4；s4g1（雙胞胎先後換心）是新聞報導，genre 標 news，sdgs 標 3；s4g2（博物館拒絕歸還古文物）genre 標 news，sdgs 標 11（文化遺產）；s4g4（四本童書的書目簡介）genre 標 other，text_format 標 multi_text。第17題「One … Another requirement …」為代名詞列舉，grammar_point 標 pronoun；第19題「aged two or three」為 aged＋年齡，標 participle；第28題「both … and …」標 correlative_conjunction；第36題「which have since perished」中 since 當副詞搭配現在完成式，標 tense（以上皆非 schema 範例值）。第44題要從 Alfred 換到 19 歲的心臟推知「younger」的原因，標 inference；第50題問 NEITHER … NOR …（兩者都沒有提到的用途），標 not_mentioned；第54題由 Plains Indians 對應 Native Americans，標 detail；第55題要把 The Table Where Rich People Sit 的簡介歸納為「金錢不是衡量財富的唯一方式」，標 inference。
